notes.title: The scouring engine. Buildings destruction in RTS. Tiny Teams Fest!
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/fb793a75d8985858685dc1a96773317041c9c6fc.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Hello orcs and humans![/b][/p][p]We are taking part in TinyTeam fest! [/p][p]To celebrate, I'm writing a short article about how destructibility works in our engine.[/p][p]I've been working on my RTS game for about 3 years, using my personal game engine, and one of the things I'm really happy with is the way buildings are demolished, have a look 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/80df13bdf1ef0c7d2a7c969ddc863292dd8fbf61.gif"][/img][/p][p]We are a very small team, so I had some important conditions for destruction system[/p][list][*][p]It need to be easy to set up, because we don't have time and resources to i.e. decompose meshes and then animate them[/p][/*][*][p]It need to be reliable because I can't be coming back to it once it's done[/p][/*][*][p]It need to look cool and make my game stand out among dozens of other RTS games[/p][/*][/list][p]Those points are especially important because we expect the community to make mods for our game, and our destruction solution should work out of the box for them.[/p][p]So here's how it's done in The Scouring.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Part 1. Setup[/b][/p][p]All the artist need to do is attach mesh blobs to parts of the building that he wants to come off, like this[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/f82207cc0d4638fa5db4fee2e01851224ae2cdcf.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We use about 100-150 blobs for buildings, and it takes just a couple of hours to set them up.[/p][p]And that's it.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Part 2. Mesh Processing[/b][/p][p]Most destruction systems use geometric intersections (boolean operations) to break mesh into pieces. However, it is a very slow and complex process that generally requires the mesh to be constructed in a specific, “correct” way.[/p][p]Instead we use alpha-clipping to break the mesh into pieces.[/p][p]2.1. So the first thing is to generate blob intersections against the original mesh.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/73cb60db683db4386884755c409229c6f745f6f8.jpg"][/img][/p][p]These are our chunks that will break off the building.[/p][p]We also generate the “backsides” of each hole.[/p][p]This might be the trickiest part of the whole thing, but I would not like to go into details of it as it is very technical. Get in touch with me if you need more details.[/p][p]2.2. Next, generate a texture atlas for our building[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/771e9357f29c6461ffc979cb43c90bdfbc066138.jpg"][/img][/p][p]There are publicly available libraries that can do that, I used [/p][p][url="https://github.com/jpcy/xatlas"]https://github.com/jpcy/xatlas[/url][/p][p]For an RTS camera and a building like that, 512x512 atlas has enough accuracy.[/p][p]2.3. Iterate every pixel in the atlas, and mark it with chunk id when the corresponding 3d position on the building surface is within one of the “blobs”[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/0be597b7fcce9aa9177197ca536351b9220ceb6f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This is the most time-consuming process (relatively speaking, the whole process described in this paper takes 0.25 ms on my 10 years old PC).[/p][p]The most important thing to speed things up is to assume all blobs to be “convex” (and there is no reason not to do so).[/p][p]Checking if a given point is inside a 3d convex hull is trivial. And there is a public library that generates convex hulls - [/p][p][url="https://github.com/akuukka/quickhull"]https://github.com/akuukka/quickhull[/url][/p][p][/p][p][b]Part 3. Runtime[/b][/p][p]So when a unit hits a building, we detect the chunk that is closest to the hit position, and mark it as active. Each building has a [i]texture buffer[/i] with the size of “n chunks”, storing a boolean for each chunk, whether it is active or not.[/p][p]In pixel shader, we read the texture atlas storing chunks id’s, and do a clip if this chunk is active.[/p][p]We also need to show the “backside” of a clipped hole. We render the “backsides” mesh, with the inverted logic of the check mentioned above (if a chunk is active - DON’T clip the backside).[/p][p]And of course the chunk itself. If the building is visible, we spawn a physical body for it. If not, we simply activate it in its resting position (next to the building).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/275e0b42ab275356f9bbd4b86df5d96aa74d7e29.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We only use 3 calls to draw the whole thing:[/p][olist][*][p]Building itself[/p][/*][*][p]Backsides[/p][/*][*][p]Chunks. We put all of the chunks geometry into a single geometry buffer, and use the same [i]texture buffer[/i] in pixel shader to clip-out inactive chunks.[/p][/*][/olist][p]When the building is being repaired, instead of activating the chunks, we deactivate them.[/p][p]Last (but not least) a few notes about additional effects.[/p][p]We separate the building into “burnable” and “static” parts. [/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/649dad2230f219f2011921e294c313737879126f.gif"][/img][/p][p]The “burnable” part slides down when the building is destroyed, and has some fancy shader effects applied to. The “static” parts simply dissolves (using a screen-space per-pixel technique)[/p][p][/p][p][b]Thank you for reading![/b][/p][p]If you have any questions, please fire at [/p][p][url="https://orcboss@orcgroupstudio.com"]orcboss@orcgroupstudio.com[/url][/p][p][/p][p][b]Pavel Zagrebelnyy[/b], Orc Boss[/p][p]&& Game Director[/p][p]&& The only one Сode Developer[/p]

notes.title: The Scouring Editor is LIVE and available for creative use.
notes.notes:
[p]We’ve seen incredible community engagement since Demo launch, and we’ve noticed that some players have started to create and share mods for The Scouring Demo. I wanted to make a game that was moddable from the start (this is why our game pack files are not encrypted, for example). It's always a pleasure for me, as a developer, to see what our community can create. Mods are great, and they will no doubt contribute to this game's longevity.[/p][p][b]Current Features:[/b][/p][p]✅ [b]Map Editor[/b] – Design your own battlefields.
✅ [b]Scripting (LUA, AI, Scenarios)[/b] – Bring your mechanics to life.
✅ [b]XML Configs[/b] – Tweak units, factions, buildings, items, and more.[/p][p][b]How to Access:[/b][/p][p]🔗 [url="https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1iQwy2Pf2amKIe4lxRz2Sr-dd9S3qdEsP"]https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1iQwy2Pf2amKIe4lxRz2Sr-dd9S3qdEsP[/url]
⚠️ [b]Note:[/b] Publishing mods to the Steam Workshop requires [b]beta access[/b] to [i]The Scouring[/i].[/p][p][b]Usefull guides:[/b][/p][p][url="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VIe3KW0Oh_rbHUqahPUXWHZ6JqGNoP4xoDsC7knyHno/edit?tab=t.0"]THE SCOURING MAP EDITOR BASIC GUIDE[/url][/p][p][url="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kPBo43G2tC7rxWjugUL_Mjah3cuzI1yKAX5syQAl_Z8/edit?tab=t.0"]THE SCOURING MODDING BASIC GUIDE[/url][/p][p][b]Beta Key Requests:[/b][/p][p]Want to share your creations? Here’s how it works:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Show Voply proof[/b] (e.g., a screenshot of your map/mod) in Discord[/p][/*][*][p][b]He’ll DM you a beta key[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Upload to the Workshop[/b] and let the community play![/p][/*][/olist][p][b]Multiplayer Note:[/b][/p][p]Custom multiplayer games will go live with [b]Early Access on August 14[/b]. Stay tuned![/p][p][/p][p][b]Pavel Zagrebelnyy[/b], Orc Boss[/p][p]&& Game Director[/p][p]&& The only one Сode Developer[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45336060/eac4a94d207c76d69168c085d8121db38889845e.jpg"][/img][/p]
